newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SPOT PRODUCTS--GASOLINE DIFFS UP, NYMEX EASES.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SPOT PRODUCTS--GASOLINE DIFFS UP, NYMEX EASES.

text.p: Gasoline differentials in both New York Harbor and the U.S. Gulf firmed modestly by late Thursday, though outright prices slid lower as the NYMEX basis price weakened.
On the NYMEX, September gasoline futures fell 1.73 cents to settle at 64.33 cents a gallon and September heating oil shed 1.68 cents to finish at 55.30 cents a gallon.
NEW YORK HARBOR
M2 conventional unleaded gasoline differentials continued to firm in moderate activity on Thursday, pushed up by what traders said were extremely tight supplies.
Prompt M2 differentials were talked at 5.25/5.50 cents over the print, about 1.25 cents above Wednesday.

A2 reformulated northern-grade gasoline shed some ground on talk that a trader had nominated a good deal of supply from the U.S. Gulf to the Harbor. Prompt A2 was down about a half cent at 7.25/7.50 cents a gallon.
"The supply may take some of the heat off the gas," said a trader.
On the distillate side, an electricity-supply company was heard looking for a small piece heating oil for loading tomorrow. Offers were at -0.75 cent under the screen.
Prompt low sulphur diesel was about 0.10 cent higher at 0.25/0.50 cents over.
U.S. GULF
Conventional M1 gasoline differentials firmed modestly on the day, though levels did dip modestly from the midday highs, according to traders.

Prompt conventional M1 changed hands at 0.25 cent over the September NYMEX near midday, a gain of about 0.75 cent on the day. However, players put those barrels at about even with the futures by the end of the day.
Any-month barrels of M1 were talked between 2.65 and 2.85 cents under the September futures.
Part of the strength was attributed to the modest cut in refinery runs at Valero and Citgo refineries in Corpus Christi, Texas because of power supply problems there.
However, the market did not appear to feel threatened by PDVSA's force majeure of nine gasoline cargoes due to refinery output problems, according to Gulf traders.
Distillate differentials weakened by the end of the day, with prompt low sulphur diesel trading at 1.90 cents under the September futures, while prompt heating oil traded at 2.60 cents under.
MIDCONTINENT
Unleaded gasoline differentials continued their downturn, caught in a vacuum of no interest. Players said Group Three unleaded fell another quarter cent after losing 0.75 cent this morning.
The range was pegged 3.25/3.50 cents over the print.
Chicago unleaded was also down at 3.25/3.50 cents, with the any months at 1.00/1.25 cents over.
